title: Valid device-token registration appears to persist data while returning a client error
reasoning: The route is the public registration endpoint, and the associated test for valid token creation explicitly notes that the view returns 400 Bad Request while still creating the DeviceToken. That is a broken API contract: clients will reasonably treat registration as failed even though server state changed, which can trigger retries, confusing UX, and duplicate or stale client-side registration flows. The test currently accepts the side effect without asserting a success status, so it documents the bad behavior instead of preventing it.
recommendation: Change DeviceTokenCreateView so a valid registration returns an appropriate 2xx response, typically 201 Created for a new token or 200 OK when updating/reassigning an existing token. Keep invalid payloads returning 400.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The valid-create test only checks that the database row exists and does not assert the response status. Its comment explicitly works around the 400 response.
suggestedRegressionTest: Update test_create_token to assert response.status_code is HTTP_201_CREATED or HTTP_200_OK for valid token data, and add the same assertion to ownership reassignment if that path should be successful.
minimumFixScope: DeviceTokenCreateView response handling for successful serializer save/create paths, plus assertions in notifications/tests/test_device_tokens.py.
